contexts.text: Those are called creatures, to whom the Gospel is to be preached, because they are to be created anew (). AR 290:2.
A new creature, or that they have received new life from the Lord. Signified.
The creatures in the sea having souls () = scientific truths with goods. AE 513, Explained.
This is meant by that the old man with his concupiscences must die, in order that man may become a new creature.
Creatures () = those who are in doctrinal things of truth.
The new creation of man is his reformation; hence a new creature is a reformed man.

There died the third part of those creatures in the sea which had souls () = that those who have lived and do live that faith, cannot be reformed and receive life... Creatures = those who can be reformed.

As affections and perceptions there appear in the forms of animals or creatures on the earth, which are called beasts; of creatures in the air, which are called birds; and of creatures in the sea, which are called fishes; beasts, birds, and fishes are so often mentioned in the Word. Illustrated.
So far man is spiritual, and is a new creature. TCR 572.
A baptized, that is, a regenerate person, is meant by a creature (; ); and by a new creature (; ); for a creature is so called from create, by which is signified to regenerate. SE 4837.
Every creature () = all who receive the Gospel, and thereby can be reformed. Others are not meant by creatures, because they do not receive.
Every creature () = both Angels and men.
The beginning of the creature of God ()... Creatures, here, = those who can be created anew, that is, regenerated, and thus become of the Lord's Church. Illustrated.
